userStories.title: P1.6b (also closes the P1.3 remainder): truthful async post-install completion — root-cause and fix the seed-0-rows hook failure and the "succeeded (delegated)" over-report
userStories.description: As a workspace owner, I want the setup operation's post-install sample-seeding step to actually seed its rows and to report failure truthfully, so that I am never told a preset succeeded when it silently seeded nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN.md P1.6b verbatim (governing bullet): "implement one authorized, resumable setup operation from preset + checkbox choices. Test same-key retries/concurrent requests, async post-install completion, registration failure and partial results; no fake completed preset or duplicate seeds."

PLAN.md P1.3 verbatim (related open remainder): "Complete preset orchestration through existing server service (not a new logic-function): partial-state reporting, owned navigation and optional samples; partial states + delegated sample-seeding step shipped (spec 15/15)." — the recorded failure to close: "live scratch shows app post-install hooks completing while seeding 0 rows (phase-01-report 2026-09-16 orchestrator entry) — 'succeeded (delegated)' can over-report until the hook failure is fixed"

The root cause of "hook completes per queue metrics but seeds 0 rows" is identified at code level and documented in the phase report (phase-04-report 2026-09-16 20:40 entry records this as the item gating populated-install proofs for P7.0 and P1.6d)

The fix is unit-proven: a test exercises the post-install/delegated seeding path and asserts rows are written (or, if the defect is only reproducible live, the instrumented fix plus a unit test of the corrected write path, with the live seed proof explicitly recorded as Tier 2)

The delegated sample-seeding step can no longer report `succeeded (delegated)` when the hook wrote 0 rows: step status reflects the actual outcome (failed/partial with safe, localized error information per C2), and a completed preset is never reported when seeding failed
Work happens in the existing WorkspaceTemplateService/post-install path — no second seeding system, no new logic-function, no duplicate of the P1.6d Bilan starter payloads

userStories.title: P1.6b: resumable setup operation — idempotency key, same-key retry and concurrent-request dedupe
userStories.description: As a workspace owner retrying a setup operation, I want the same operation key to never create duplicate apps, defaults or seeds even under retries or simultaneous requests, so that retrying is always safe.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN.md P1.6b verbatim (governing bullet): "implement one authorized, resumable setup operation from preset + checkbox choices. Test same-key retries/concurrent requests, async post-install completion, registration failure and partial results; no fake completed preset or duplicate seeds."
Same operation key retried N times produces exactly one set of installed apps, owned defaults and seeds — asserted by unit test (no duplicate seeds, no double install)
Concurrent requests carrying the same key resolve to one operation execution (others join or return the same operation result) — asserted by unit test

The operation exposes a stable operation ID and per-step status (`pending/running/succeeded/failed/skipped` per C2 §4) that survives a retry; installed application state remains the truth source (the progress record is not a second activation table)
Caller identity is server-derived, not trusted from input; authorize workspace configuration with existing permissions (C2)
Implemented by extending the existing WorkspaceTemplateService operation path and the apply-template-operation.types.ts contracts (P1.6a, commit 9b50ab87) — no parallel operation system
Tier 0 gate — diff lint: `npx nx lint:diff-with-main twenty-server` clean (direct `npx oxlint --type-aware` + `npx oxfmt --check` on touched files is the covering gate while uncommitted)
Tier 0 gate — typecheck: `npx tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes inside packages/twenty-server
Tier 0/1 gate — targeted tests: `npx jest <touched-spec> --config=packages/twenty-server/jest.config.mjs` passes for every spec the story adds or edits

Tier 2 stays with the orchestrator: no `yarn start`, no live scratch workspace run; a dated executor entry is appended to docs/plan/phases/phase-01-report.md; PLAN.md is not edited; nothing is committed

userStories.title: P1.6b: registration failure and partial results — keep successful work, surface exactly what failed, resume with revalidation
userStories.description: As a workspace owner whose setup operation partially failed, I want the successful steps kept, the failed step named with a safe error, and a resume that revalidates permissions and versions, so that I can retry without losing work or re-running what already succeeded.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN.md P1.6b verbatim (governing bullet): "implement one authorized, resumable setup operation from preset + checkbox choices. Test same-key retries/concurrent requests, async post-install completion, registration failure and partial results; no fake completed preset or duplicate seeds."

A registration/install failure mid-operation keeps all successful steps, marks the failed step with safe localized error/retry information, and never reports the entire preset applied (C2: "Partial failure keeps successful work, shows exactly what failed, allows retry/skip optional steps, and never reports the entire preset applied")
Retry after failure resumes the same operation without redoing succeeded steps, and revalidates permissions and versions on resume
Unit tests cover the failure/partial/resume paths against the P1.6a contract shapes (docs/plan/05-template-contracts.md §4–§6; fixtures exist from the P1.6a PRD US-003)
Optional steps can be skipped without discarding the operation result; unavailable optional apps are excluded rather than failing the bundle

userStories.title: P3.2 (sharing, bullet 5): owner-side share-management UX — display/copy URL, passphrase field, expiry picker, revoke
userStories.description: As a document owner, I want to create a share link with an optional passphrase and expiry, see and copy the /share/<token> URL, and revoke it, so that I can share snapshots safely without touching the API.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN.md P3.2 verbatim (governing bullet): "Repair public snapshot sharing: record-level rights, validated plaintext or ciphertext-only representation, consistent guest format, display/copy URL, revoke, expiry and passphrase UX. P0.2 gates E05."

Scope: the record-level rights, validated representation, guest format and expiry/revoke server enforcement are already P0.2-shipped (phase-03-report 2026-09-17 snapshot-sharing entry: "Bullets 2–4 are P0.2-shipped ... covered by the existing unit/integration suites") — this slice is the recorded open leg: "bullet 5 owner-side share-management UX (display/copy URL, passphrase field, expiry picker, revoke) is not wired — document-browser.front-component.tsx's shareDocument still discards the returned token"

shareDocument no longer discards the returned token: the owner UI displays and copies the `/share/:shareToken` URL (AppPath.DocumentShare), offers an optional passphrase field and expiry picker on create, and a revoke action calling the existing workspace-scoped deleteDocumentShare

Passphrase creation reuses the existing client-side encrypt-before-upload model via a share-crypto lib ported out of twenty-front into a reusable pure module (per the report's "Next" — never move the passphrase itself over the wire)
Extend, do not duplicate: validateRepresentation (full triple XOR plaintext, bounded lengths) and the guest plaintext omission are P0.2's; the guest page and its crypto round-trip tests already exist
Pure-lib node tests for the ported crypto/helpers; unit tests for the new owner-side UI logic (create/copy/revoke state transitions)

userStories.title: P3.3 (tree, leg 1): server-side cycle validation on document move/reparent
userStories.description: As a document author, I want a move that would make a document its own ancestor to be rejected server-side with a useful error, so that the tree can never contain a cycle regardless of which client issues the write.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN.md P3.3 verbatim (governing bullet): "Finish existing document tree: lazy/paginated loading at every depth, server cycle validation, deterministic sibling ordering and accessible move controls. Verify favorites are personal rather than a shared flag; test archive/restore/purge across deep trees and more than one API page. Existing tree/drag/cron code is a starting point, not full acceptance."
Scope (phase-03-report 2026-09-18 "Next"): "server-side cycle validation on move/reparent (the first remaining tree bullet)" — this story delivers that leg only
A move/reparent that would make the target an ancestor of (or equal to) the source is rejected fail-closed with a useful, localized-safe error; the rejected write mutates nothing
Legitimate deep moves (subtree relocation to a unrelated branch) still succeed; self-parenting is rejected
Unit tests cover: direct cycle (A→B→A), deep cycle (A→B→C→A), self-parent, and a valid deep cross-branch move

Implemented on the existing app-owned document object write path (extend the existing hook/service — no second validation system); fractional indexing util in twenty-shared/utils remains the ordering primitive

userStories.title: P9.1 (assistant surface, first Tier 0/1 slice): side-panel assistant consuming the native tool registry with context injection and context buttons
userStories.description: As a user, I want an assistant panel that knows which app tools exist for my current context and offers them as buttons, so that I can use per-app AI actions without learning prompts or terminology.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN.md P9.1 verbatim (governing bullets): "Consume existing `LogicFunctionToolProvider`/tool registry and app `toolTriggerSettings`; validate install/uninstall/permissions/context behavior. P1.5 established this native primitive; do not invent `registerAiTools`, a duplicate table or manual registration hooks." and "Assistant surface: side-panel assistant + full-page upgrade of ai-chat; context injection from current view (record/doc/channel/invoice) via context-store"

Recorded seam (phase-01-report): "P9's 'registry' work reduces to consuming `ToolRegistryService.getCatalog()` / `getToolsByCategories()` in the assistant surface + any per-app gating policy" — the panel consumes that existing registry; no new registry, table or registration hook

Side-panel assistant surface renders the tools available for the current context as context buttons (the recorded "Next": "P9.1's assistant surface that renders these tools as context buttons"), reading context from the current view (record/doc/channel) via a context-store

The already-shipped per-app tools (US-009 extract-tasks, US-010 chat summarize/catch-me-up, US-011 drive find-file/dedupe-hints, US-012 standup-digest/task-breakdown, US-013 document-content) appear through the registry without any per-tool front registration

Every mutation-path tool requires explicit user confirmation before any write (C6: draft + confirm; no AI auto-posting); this slice ships read-only dispatch only — streaming responses, model provider config and usage logging remain later P9.1 bullets and are not started here
Uninstalled-app tools and tools the caller lacks permissions for are not offered (fail-closed filtering, unit-proven)
Unit tests cover registry consumption, context mapping and permission/app gating of the offered tools
